summary_paragraph: A 68-year-old woman was admitted for evaluation of progressive weakness and recurrent falls, occurring in the context of poor oral intake and overuse of diuretics. She presented with lightheadedness, exertional chest pain, and dehydration. Initial labs revealed acute kidney injury, hyponatremia, elevated lactate, and leukocytosis, all attributed to hypovolemia from excessive diuresis. An ECG showed deep T-wave inversions and a mildly elevated troponin, consistent with a Type II NSTEMI secondary to supply-demand imbalance. Imaging showed no acute intracranial or intra-abdominal processes, a stable pancreatic cyst, and no fractures. She was rehydrated with IV fluids, her torsemide dose was reduced, and metolazone was discontinued. Aspirin was resumed after hematologic consultation. Her symptoms improved, renal function normalized, and she was discharged to extended care with stable vital signs, improved strength, and a plan for outpatient follow-up.
